parts.title: The Anatomy of Tech Conference CFPs: Committee Rubrics & Selection
say: Welcome to Block 11 and Day 51! Speaking on stage at marquee software conferences—such as KubeCon, Strange Loop, QCon, GOTO, or AWS re:Invent—is the premier catalyst for building global technical reputation. When you deliver a keynote before 2,000 engineers, you are no longer just an employee at a company; you are an recognized industry authority whose insights shape how other organizations build software.

However, before you can step onto the stage, you must conquer the **Call for Proposals (CFP)** selection gauntlet. At tier-1 conferences, selection committees receive between 800 and 2,500 CFP submissions for only 40 to 60 speaking slots. Acceptance rates typically hover between 3% and 7%—more selective than admission to Ivy League universities!

parts.title: Conference Demo Risk Mitigation Toolkit: Self-Contained Offline Docker Containers
say: We have all witnessed the agonizing conference catastrophe: A brilliant speaker says, 'And now, let us run the live demo!' They switch to their terminal, execute `kubectl apply`, and... nothing happens. The venue Wi-Fi has collapsed under the weight of 2,000 attendees browsing their laptops. The terminal hangs. The speaker sweats, restarts their hotspot, apologizes four times, and burns 8 painful minutes of their talk while the audience glances at their phones.

To achieve 100% demo survivability, professional conference speakers engineer a three-layer defense-in-depth shield: Layer 1 (**Self-Contained Local Container**): Package your entire application stack—Kafka brokers, Postgres databases, mock API gateways, and web frontends—into a local `docker-compose.yml` that boots entirely on `localhost:8080` with zero external dependencies.
